findings.title: Cache key uses Python's per-process randomized hash() of a tuple
findings.body: The key is `hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids)))`. Python's built-in hash of a tuple of ints is stable, but it is a lossy 64-bit hash with possible collisions, and it makes the key opaque. Two different project sets that collide would share an eligibility result. That can wrongly upsample counts for non-allowlisted projects. Use a deterministic join of the IDs, or a real digest, instead.

findings.title: Cached eligibility is never invalidated, so allowlist changes are delayed up to 60s
findings.body: `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is defined but never called anywhere, including when the `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist` option changes. After an allowlist edit, results stay stale for 60s. That is only an option lookup, which is already cheap and in-process, so the cache adds staleness and a cache round trip with almost no benefit. The tests also mock `options` but not the cache, so a cached value from one test can leak into another via the shared cache. The cache should be removed or properly invalidated.

findings.title: Allowlist membership check on a list of raw option values
findings.body: `project_id in allowlist` is a linear scan per project and relies on the option holding ints. If the option is stored with a different type (e.g. strings), eligibility is silently False. Convert to a set of ints for both correctness and performance.

findings.title: Upsampling check uses outer `dataset`, not `scoped_dataset`
findings.body: `_get_event_stats` receives `scoped_dataset`, which differs from `dataset` in the dashboard-split paths (e.g. `discover` is passed for the errors-only query). The eligibility check passes the closure's `dataset`. In the split path the transformation can be applied or skipped for the wrong dataset. For example, a transaction-only query run against `discover` can get `upsampled_count()` even though the sample_weight column does not apply. Use `scoped_dataset`.

findings.title: Error detection is a naive substring match on the raw request query
findings.body: `_is_error_focused_query` checks `"event.type:error" in query` on the raw request `query` param. This misses `!event.type:error`, so negated queries are treated as error queries. It also misses queries that only get event.type through the split path's appended `AND !event.type:transaction`. For example, `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction` is treated as error-only and so would sum sample_weight over transactions. The query actually executed in `_get_event_stats` (the `query` argument) is not used.

findings.title: Upsampling applied to RPC datasets / transformed column not supported there
findings.body: The transformed column `upsampled_count() as count` is passed to `run_timeseries_query` and `run_top_events_timeseries_query` for the RPC path. The RPC resolver has no `upsampled_count` function. `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` returns False for other datasets, so this is mostly dead code today. It is also unreachable-looking logic that would break if the dataset check changes. The same transform is duplicated in three branches instead of being done once.

findings.title: upsampled_count sums sample_weight, which is NULL/absent for events without sample rate
findings.body: `sum(sample_weight)` ignores events with a NULL sample_weight, so events lacking a sample rate contribute 0 instead of 1. The comment assumes the column exists for every event in allowlisted projects, but nothing enforces that. Counts will be undercounted, or 0 for projects with no sample_weight. It should fall back with something like `ifNull(sample_weight, 1)`. The function also isn't validated against the errors dataset (`sample_weight` may not be a known column in the builder).

findings.title: Test factory silently swallows all exceptions and mutates event data
findings.body: `_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling` uses bare `except Exception: pass`. It also sets `sample_rate` on every stored event from the context, changing behavior of unrelated tests. Failures to parse are hidden, and a falsy rate of 0 is ignored.

findings.title: Stray submodule/gitlink file committed
findings.body: A `sentry-repo` gitlink (Subproject commit a5d29095...) was added to the repository. This looks like an accidental artifact and should not be part of the change.

findings.title: Misleading comments and trailing whitespace
findings.body: Comments claim a 'cached result ensures consistent behavior' and 'late transformation ensures most current schema assumptions', which is inaccurate. Lines 223, 234 and 278 contain trailing whitespace (lint failures). The unrelated error message change at line 124 is also bundled in.

findings.title: Tests don't cover top_events path, cache behavior, or discover dataset with errors; fragile cache interplay
findings.body: Tests mock `options` but the real cache is used. Cached eligibility keyed by org and project IDs can leak between tests and give order-dependent results. `self.project`/`project2` are created via `create_project()`, whose IDs vary, so key collisions are unlikely but not controlled. There is no coverage of topEvents or of the dashboard split path, where the dataset mismatch bug lives.
